reviewCadence: At every session cookie, CSRF token, browser-origin, CORS, fetch wrapper, login, session rotation, or authenticated mutating route change.

requirements.name: Use signed session-bound CSRF tokens
requirements.owasp: Signed double-submit cookies should bind the token to session-specific data with HMAC and reject naive unsigned tokens.

controls.name: HMAC double-submit token
controls.description: The readable CSRF cookie stores a versioned nonce plus HMAC signature bound to the opaque session cookie value.

requirements.name: Require CSRF tokens on state-changing browser requests
requirements.owasp: All state-changing requests authenticated with cookies must carry a server-validated CSRF token.

controls.name: Mutating method guard
controls.description: The account API requires the scoped CSRF cookie and matching X-CSRF-Token header for authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE requests.

requirements.name: Attach tokens from trusted browser clients
requirements.owasp: AJAX clients should send a custom CSRF header because cross-site forms cannot add arbitrary request headers.

controls.name: Shared fetch wrappers
controls.description: Typed browser fetch clients attach X-CSRF-Token on mutating credentialed requests and preserve authuser-scoped cookie selection.

requirements.name: Verify Origin and Referer
requirements.owasp: Origin and Referer validation provide defense in depth for requests that use browser credentials.

controls.name: Allowed browser origin guard
controls.description: Cookie-authenticated mutating requests must originate from configured first-party origins or registered browser OAuth redirect origins.

requirements.name: Use Fetch Metadata as defense in depth
requirements.owasp: Sec-Fetch-* headers should reject cross-site and untrusted browser request contexts where supported.

controls.name: Fetch Metadata policy
controls.description: Authenticated mutating requests reject cross-site, no-cors, and subresource destinations before token validation succeeds.

requirements.name: Harden session and CSRF cookies
requirements.owasp: SameSite cookies, Secure, HttpOnly for session cookies, and host-prefixed names reduce ambient cookie abuse.

controls.name: Strict first-party cookies
controls.description: Session cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure in non-development, and host-prefixed; CSRF cookies are readable but SameSite=Strict and host-prefixed.

requirements.name: Constrain credentialed CORS
requirements.owasp: Credentialed cross-origin requests must only be allowed for trusted origins and custom CSRF headers must be allowed explicitly.

controls.name: Trusted-origin CORS
controls.description: CORS reflects only registered same-origin matches, allows credentials only for those origins, and permits X-CSRF-Token for preflighted API requests.

requirements.name: Keep bearer-token endpoints outside cookie CSRF scope
requirements.owasp: APIs authenticated without ambient browser cookies should avoid unnecessary CSRF token coupling while retaining origin controls for browser flows.

controls.name: Explicit OAuth skip list
controls.description: OAuth token, introspection, revocation, and pushed-authorization endpoints are excluded from cookie CSRF middleware because they are client-authenticated protocol endpoints.

requirements.name: Prevent CSRF control regressions
requirements.owasp: CSRF defenses should be tested and kept in automated checks so future route and client changes cannot silently remove controls.

controls.name: CSRF prevention gate
controls.description: The root check path validates signed token generation, middleware enforcement, Fetch Metadata, Origin/Referer, cookie attributes, CORS, client token attachment, and tests.
